utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: Hello Patricia. Thank you for coming in today. How are you holding up?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: It's been a hard week. Three years ago today my mother passed away. I'm just sad. Not like dangerously sad, just missing her. I had a good cry this morning.

utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: Anniversary grief is real and valid. Honoring that sadness is healthy. Can you tell me what you miss most about her?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Her laugh. The way she'd call every Sunday morning. I feel her absence most at family dinners. My kids ask about grandma and it's bittersweet to talk about her.

utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: It sounds like she was a wonderful presence. How do your kids handle those conversations?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Really well actually. My youngest made a little memory box with photos and drawings. I cried but in a good way. I feel like keeping her memory alive is the right approach.

utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: That's a beautiful ritual. Memorial practices are psychologically very healthy. Are you taking care of yourself this week?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Trying to. I went for a walk this morning, called my sister to remember mom together. I feel like I miss her but I'm okay. Life goes on and she'd want me to be happy.

utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: It sounds like you have a healthy relationship with her memory. That takes time and work to build. You should be proud.
